![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/00e09ca44feb1fcfa5d3ece010a858dbd98efe57985b0f8d5210f9d98a02f498.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}{y}^{2}\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the top one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/9002d6f1e55a734e410fc85111816294ed037c4a4139e9bc8bceb53c62daeeb6.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 1+x},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/31f2ff96afa1248427c1a6dd5074c47190c70983d7c0d5dfdd3def8bd883aef8.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1+x}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1+x}{y}^{2}\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1+x}{y}^{2}\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1+x}{y}^{2}\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{y}^{2}z]_{z=0}^{z=1+x}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}(1+x)\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}(1+x)\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{2}(1+x){y}^{2}\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(1+x){[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(1+x)(\frac{8}{3}-0)\,dx \\  & =\frac{8}{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}1+x\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}1+x\,dx & =\frac{8}{3}{[x+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}(3+\frac{9}{2})-0 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
